definitions.explanation: The wife of a king. Refers to a queen by marriage rather than a queen regnant who rules in her own right. Used in historical and literary contexts.

examples.japanese: {王后|おうごう}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{国民|こくみん}→国民：02757_kokumin⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{愛|あい}されていた→愛する：01811_aisuru⟧。
examples.english: The queen was loved by the people.

examples.japanese: ⟦{王|おう}→王：19353_ou⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧{王后|おうごう}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{並|なら}んで→並ぶ：00605_narabu⟧{玉座|ぎょくざ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{座|すわ}った→座る：00757_suwaru⟧。
examples.english: The king and queen sat side by side on the throne.

examples.japanese: {歴史書|れきししょ}⟦によると→〜によると：03104_niyoruto⟧、⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧{王后|おうごう}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{政治|せいじ}→政治：01629_seiji⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{大|おお}きな→大きな：02849_ookina⟧⟦{影響力|えいきょうりょく}→影響力：20040_eikyouryoku⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{持|も}っていた→持つ：00478_motsu⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦されている→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: According to historical records, this queen consort is said to have also had great political influence.

notes:
A compound of ⟦{王|おう}→王：19353_ou⟧ (king) and {后|ごう} (consort, empress). {后|ごう} specifically denotes a female royal consort. In Japanese historical texts, {后|きさき} is also used to refer to an emperor's wife.

In modern contexts, ⟦{王妃|おうひ}→王妃：13634_ouhi⟧ is more commonly used to refer to a queen consort of a foreign country.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{王|おう}→王：19353_ou⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧{王后|おうごう}: king and queen
- {王后|おうごう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{座|ざ}→座：28170_za⟧: the position of queen
- {王后|おうごう}⟦として→として：06802_toshite⟧⟦{即位|そくい}→即位：11974_sokui⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to be enthroned as queen
- {王后|おうごう}⟦{陛下|へいか}→陛下：14566_heika⟧: Her Majesty the Queen

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{王妃|おうひ}→王妃：13634_ouhi⟧: queen consort, princess — more commonly used in modern contexts for foreign royalty
- ⟦{女王|じょおう}→女王：03349_joou⟧: queen regnant — a female ruler in her own right
- ⟦{皇后|こうごう}→皇后：16354_kougou⟧: empress consort — specifically the wife of an emperor, used for the Japanese empress
